items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-07-21
items.q: I was an escort for Louis Armstrong in 1949 when he was a king because I drove one of the automobiles for him and I was an escort for his wife also.

ctx.x: This was in the 40s and into the 50s. You know, New Orleans had, beside being noted number one for jazz and blues and whatnot. We were first in a lot of things, in sports and things Now you're talking about baseball, I always see the photo of Louis Armstrong with his

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-08-23
items.q: The world's greatest ambassador, Louis Armstrong, who came to New Orleans many a time in the 1930s. He played that concert.

ctx.x: Did that cause the demise of that club? Because I don't think it...

I don't think so. No. No. I don't think it caused the demise of the club. I think things started changing with... You see, Club Desire was down in the Ninth Ward. But you had the Dewdrop, the Robin Hood, and all of these Johnny-come-lately clubs, which were just beginning to hit their stride to develop new entertainment. Then, like I said, you had the Coliseum Arena, which was in the central part of the city. You had the ILA Club, which was in the French Quarter. You had all of these things jumping against…
How do you see the difference? Is there any difference between rhythm and blues and rock and roll? I mean, did you see a difference?

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: but we got together and owned a couple of affairs and we had a couple of social visits

ctx.x: Yeah. Now, did you cover Louis when he came back in 65?

Did you cover that? I didn't officially cover Louis as such, but we got together and owned a couple of affairs and we had a couple of social visits, but I didn't do the writing or did the covering at that time. Other people were doing things because I was doing some other things. And if I, in 65, I'll tell you what I did do. I put his coming to New Orleans on the air because I was doing a newscasting. I might have a tape on it also because I used to tape a lot of my programs on Louis Armstrong. In fact, I said,…
My question was is that I've read, I don't know, wasn't it in the weekly that the black press kind of got shut out of coverage, that they had problems getting access to Louis when he came back

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: There I was right there emceeing these shows. I emceed for two or three times that Louis Armstrong came to New Orleans.

ctx.x: How'd you get to be Louis' escort?

I don't know, it just, I tell you what happened. By being in radio and working for a newspaper, here I'm a press man. And everybody in the Zulu Club at that time, they knew me. Especially Ernest Wright who thought the world of me. I was a big name person in New Orleans because he was affiliated with a lot of unions and with churches and so forth and so on. So between Ernest Wright and Jim Russell and Jim Poole who was a big wheel in the Zulus at that particular time. God bless him. So that's how I got to become…
Yeah, that was, yeah. That's about all it would have been.
